title: Customer Insights - Data: MCP server grounds agents in unified customer profiles and insights
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, gateway provisioning and consent, scoped registry blocking, and billing qualifications are supported by Microsoft documentation. The Entra consent route is correct but omits the Manage heading on the app registration page; this is a minor navigation correction.

claims.claim: The Customer Insights MCP server exposes Customer Insights capabilities as callable tools for agents and chat clients.
claims.quote: The Customer Insights Model Context Protocol (MCP) server exposes Dynamics 365 Customer Insights - Data and select Customer Insights - Journeys capabilities as callable tools for LLM agents.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio agents and other HTTP-based MCP clients can connect to the server.
claims.quote: Use the Dynamics 365 CX Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server - Customer Insights to connect Customer Insights data and tools to Microsoft Copilot Studio agents, or to any other MCP client that supports HTTP-based MCP connections.

claims.claim: Makers add an available MCP server to each agent they choose.
claims.quote: Each MCP server in Copilot Studio is a tool that you can add to your agent. When you add the MCP server to your agent as a tool, the server appears as a tool on the agent's Tools tab.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The registry Block control is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Registry > MCP server > Block.
claims.quote: In the left navigation pane, select Agents > Tools > Registry. Select actions directly from the list, or select a tool to view its overview page. Block | Prevents the selected tool from being used by agents or workflows.

claims.claim: No API or automation operation is documented for this registered server's tenant registry Block control.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Agents Tools Registry block MCP server Microsoft Graph API; MCP block graph.microsoft.com tools registry; Microsoft 365 tools registry MCP block API PowerShell beta aiInteraction tool governance. Read Tools overview and management excerpts; no matching operation.

claims.where: controls[0].note; summary; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Registry blocking governs supported Agent 365 experiences, not necessarily every product or connected component.
claims.quote: Microsoft Agent 365 provides administrative controls for supported tools. Copilot Studio and Power Platform can have separate controls for their components. An approval or block doesn't necessarily apply across all products or connected components.

claims.claim: Registry actions include both Block and Unblock.
claims.quote: Block | Prevents the selected tool from being used by agents or workflows. Unblock | Restores access to a previously blocked tool.

claims.claim: Per-agent MCP tool selection is at Copilot Studio (maker) > Tools > select the MCP server > Tools > Allow all.
claims.quote: Go to the Tools tab for your agent. Select the MCP server from the list of tools. Tools: A list of names and descriptions for the MCP tools that the server offers. Turn off the Allow all toggle.

claims.claim: No API operation is documented for the per-agent Allow all or individual MCP tool toggles.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio MCP Allow all individual tool toggle API Dataverse botcomponent entity reference; botcomponent MCP tools selection. Read MCP selection, MCP management, and botcomponent reference; searched botcomponent for MCP, Allow all and tool selection/enabling: no matching setting.

claims.claim: The cited Copilot Studio MCP tool-selection instructions describe the standard harness.
claims.quote: This article describes features used in agents or agent flows powered by the standard harness.

claims.claim: The maker-side tool toggles configure the selected individual agent.
claims.quote: If you don't want to use all the tools offered by an MCP server, you can selectively turn off MCP server tools directly in your agent.

claims.claim: Turning off Allow all enables individual toggles for selecting tools.
claims.quote: Turn off the Allow all toggle. Toggles become available for each of the individual tools. Use the individual toggles to turn off tools that aren't needed to ensure your agent only uses the most relevant features.

claims.claim: Tool-selection changes require Save and Publish to affect the agent.
claims.quote: Select Save. To make newly added or removed tools available to the agent, select Publish.

claims.claim: New server tools stay off by default after Allow all is turned off.
claims.quote: When you turn off Allow all, any new tools added to the MCP server are turned off by default.

claims.claim: New-MgServicePrincipal -AppId "<ATG-app-id>" provisions the gateway service principal.
claims.quote: As a tenant admin, run one of the following commands. New-MgServicePrincipal -AppId "<ATG-app-id>". Microsoft Entra creates the Agent 365 Tooling Gateway service principal under Enterprise applications in the customer tenant.

claims.claim: A portal UI route for provisioning the gateway service principal is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Agent 365 Tooling Gateway provision service principal tenant Microsoft Entra admin center UI; Agent 365 Tooling Gateway Enterprise applications New application. Read Data gateway page and Journeys provisioning excerpts; commands and consent URLs, but no provisioning UI route.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The gateway provisioning instructions require a tenant admin.
claims.quote: As a tenant admin, run one of the following commands.

claims.claim: az ad sp create --id <ATG-app-id> is the documented alternative provisioning command.
claims.quote: As a tenant admin, run one of the following commands. az ad sp create --id <ATG-app-id>

claims.claim: Creating the service principal and granting permission consent to a client app are separate actions.
claims.quote: Run the commands in this section instead. If you set the server up manually, grant admin consent on your own client app, as described later in this article.

claims.claim: The Entra client-app permission path begins at Entra ID > App registrations and ends at Grant admin consent.
claims.quote: Browse to Entra ID > App registrations and select New registration. Select API permissions under Manage on your app registration's Overview page.
claims.fix: In controls[3].ui and its rendered table, use 'Entra ID > App registrations > client app > Manage > API permissions > Add a permission > APIs my organization uses > Agent 365 Tooling Gateway (search by app ID) > McpServers.D365CustomerInsights.All (delegated permission) > Grant admin consent'. Manage is the omitted heading, not a different route. The navigation is at https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity-platform/quickstart-register-app and the permission steps are at the existing gateway citation.

claims.claim: On the client app, the gateway permission steps are API permissions > Add a permission > APIs my organization uses > gateway app > delegated permission > Grant admin consent.
claims.quote: Go to API permissions, and then select Add a permission. Select APIs my organization uses. Search for the Agent 365 Tooling Gateway app by using the app ID. Add the McpServers.D365CustomerInsights.All delegated permission. Select Grant admin consent.

claims.claim: The printed v2.0 admin-consent URL targets the client app with the gateway /.default scope and registered redirect URI.
claims.quote: https://login.microsoftonline.com/<customer-tenant-id>/v2.0/adminconsent?client_id=<your-client-app-id>&scope=<ATG-app-id>/.default&redirect_uri=<redirect-uri-registered-on-your-app>

claims.claim: Manual setup or connecting an external MCP client requires tenant admin or delegated admin-consent permissions.
claims.quote: Tenant admin or delegated admin-consent permissions, to set up the server manually or to connect an external MCP client

claims.claim: The permission and admin-consent URL belong to the administrator's client app, not the gateway app.
claims.quote: If you prefer a consent URL to the portal, use the v2.0 admin-consent endpoint and point it at your client app, not at the gateway app.

claims.claim: The capability is admin-opt-in because the tenant gateway service principal must be provisioned before clients can obtain tokens.
claims.quote: Before a client app can request a token for it, the gateway service principal must exist in the customer tenant. As a tenant admin, run one of the following commands.

claims.claim: The mixed licensing classification combines licensed Customer Insights with metered Copilot Studio agent usage.
claims.quote: When you purchase a Copilot Studio license, you get a specific number of billed Copilot Credits. You pool this capacity across the entire tenant.

claims.claim: MCP is Model Context Protocol, a standardized mechanism for exposing tools to agents.
claims.quote: Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. MCP servers | Standardized servers that expose tools and resources an agent can dynamically discover and use.

claims.claim: An agent can resolve Dataverse contacts and leads to unified customer profiles.
claims.quote: Resolves a unified customer ID from a Dataverse contact GUID. Call list_data_sources first to find valid source entity names, such as contact, lead, or a custom table.

claims.claim: The profile tools retrieve Customer Insights - Data segment membership.
claims.quote: get_customer_segments | Get Customer Segments | Lists the Customer Insights - Data segments a customer belongs to

claims.claim: The profile tools retrieve calculated measures.
claims.quote: get_customer_measures | Get Customer Measures | Returns calculated measures and KPIs

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The profile tools retrieve predictions including churn probability and customer lifetime value.
claims.quote: Returns machine learning predictions for a unified customer, such as churn probability, predicted lifetime value, propensity scores, and next-best-product suggestions.

claims.claim: The profile tools return cluster membership, including households.
claims.quote: get_cluster_information | Get Cluster Information | Returns cluster membership, such as a household, and other members

claims.claim: To add the catalog server, use the agent's Tools page > Add a tool > MCP filter and search Dynamics 365 CX Customer Insights.
claims.quote: Go to the Tools page for your agent, and then select Add a tool. Select the MCP filter. Search for Dynamics 365 CX Customer Insights.

claims.claim: Learn documents external connections for Visual Studio Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor, ChatGPT and Claude Code.
claims.quote: Connect supported external MCP clients, such as Visual Studio Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor, ChatGPT, and Claude Code

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: All tools requiring Customer Insights - Data are read-only.
claims.quote: create_journey is the only tool that writes data. It isn't read-only, destructive, or idempotent, so calling it twice creates two journeys. Every other tool only reads.

claims.claim: One MCP server serves both Customer Insights - Data and Customer Insights - Journeys.
claims.quote: One MCP server serves both Customer Insights - Data and Customer Insights - Journeys, but each tool works with a specific app.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: create_journey writes a Customer Insights - Journeys journey record.
claims.quote: Validates a complete journey JSON payload, enriches it, validates the enriched payload again, and then creates the Customer Insights - Journeys journey record.

claims.claim: Learn already documents the server and connection steps despite the roadmap's In development status.
claims.quote: Configure a Copilot Studio agent to use the server through Agent 365 Tooling Gateway. Connect supported external MCP clients, such as Visual Studio Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor, ChatGPT, and Claude Code

claims.claim: Unified profiles combine Dataverse records with external information such as contract and loyalty data.
claims.quote: Customer Insights - Data matches the lead and contact records and creates a unified customer profile that combines Dynamics 365 data with external contract data.

claims.claim: Catalog availability follows registration approval and required Microsoft Entra consent.
claims.quote: For MCP servers, registration approval and required Microsoft Entra consent are separate steps. The server becomes available to agent-building surfaces only after consent is granted.

claims.claim: Customer profile tools read Dataverse virtual entities reflecting live unified Customer Insights - Data.
claims.quote: They read from Dataverse virtual entities, which reflect the live unified customer data that Customer Insights - Data creates, including its segments, measures, predictions, and clusters.

claims.claim: Profile details include source records and identification of the source contributing each winning unified value.
claims.quote: Each source record includes the non-system attributes from the source entity, how those attributes map to unified profile attributes, and a flag that identifies which source contributed the winning value for each unified field.

claims.claim: get_customer_details returns personal profile data that can be included in an agent response.
claims.quote: Returns a complete Customer 360 view for one unified customer. The result includes: Core profile attributes, such as name, email, and address, with system columns excluded

claims.claim: Connections to Microsoft or external non-Dynamics services allow data to leave the Dynamics 365 FedRAMP High boundary.
claims.quote: Enabling connections between Dynamics 365 and non-Dynamics 365 services, including Microsoft or external services, allows data to leave the Dynamics 365 FedRAMP High boundary.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft asks the tenant administrator to confirm connection security, compliance, residency and governance before enabling connections.
claims.quote: Before you enable MCP server connections for your organization, your tenant administrator should confirm that these connections meet your data security, compliance, residency, and governance requirements.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Tools enforce authorization in the caller's user context.
claims.quote: Authorization is enforced inside the tool logic using the caller's user context.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Row-level security restricts the customer data a caller can reach.
claims.quote: Data-level security | Row-level security makes sure users only reach data they're authorized to see

claims.claim: Each tool checks relevant entity-specific privileges.
claims.quote: Tool-level authorization | Each tool checks entity-specific privileges, such as read access to consent purposes

claims.claim: The server never implicitly escalates privileges.
claims.quote: The MCP server never escalates privileges implicitly. Tools act as facades and never do anything beyond what the calling user is permitted to do.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Change & support
claims.claim: Missing tools can result from the calling user lacking underlying Dataverse table privileges.
claims.quote: Tools are missing from the agent | The calling user lacks privileges for the underlying Dataverse tables | Check the user's security role privileges.

claims.claim: The documented connections use the OAuth-protected Agent 365 Tooling Gateway.
claims.quote: Agent 365 Tooling Gateway is an OAuth 2.0-protected resource.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The /.default scope requires advance admin consent.
claims.quote: The /.default scope doesn't support incremental or dynamic user consent, so admin consent must be granted in advance in the customer tenant.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Users can consent to McpServers.D365CustomerInsights.All themselves if tenant user consent is allowed.
claims.quote: The named permission is user-consentable, so each person can consent for themselves if your tenant allows user consent.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Each external client signs in with its own Entra client app, whose permission to call the gateway must be allowed.
claims.quote: Each of these clients signs in with its own Microsoft Entra client app, so a tenant admin still needs to allow that client to call the gateway.

claims.claim: create_journey is not idempotent.
claims.quote: create_journey is the only tool in the Customer Insights MCP Server that creates data. It isn't idempotent, so retrying a failed call can create a duplicate journey.

claims.claim: A server URL missing /mcp/environments/ returns 404 RouteNotFound.
claims.quote: The /mcp/environments/ path segment is required. If you leave it out, the request returns 404 RouteNotFound.

claims.claim: Using a tenant ID instead of the environment ID in the server URL causes 400 EndpointInvalid.
claims.quote: 400 EndpointInvalid, with the message Environment id ... is invalid. | The /environments/ segment holds a tenant ID or a malformed GUID | Use the Dataverse environment ID, not the tenant ID.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: A gateway token lacking the Customer Insights delegated permission can cause 403 Forbidden.
claims.quote: A client can have a valid gateway token and still get 403 Forbidden from the MCP server. If calls are denied, decode the token and check that the scp claim contains McpServers.D365CustomerInsights.All.

claims.claim: Each environment needs its own connector configuration because the server URL is environment-specific.
claims.quote: The server URL is specific to the environment, so each environment needs its own connector configuration.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Licence; Scope: Users and licences
claims.claim: The feature overview's only prerequisite is user access to Dataverse tables, and it names no MCP server license.
claims.quote: Prerequisites: The user must have access to the Dataverse tables.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Employee-facing Copilot Studio agents and invoked tools are included in the Microsoft Copilot USL when the user is licensed and the agent uses that authenticated user's identity.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio agents and Copilot Studio tools and features that these agents invoke are included in the Microsoft Copilot USL when the user of the agent is licensed with Microsoft Copilot, and the agent operates using the authenticated Microsoft Copilot USL user's identity.

claims.claim: That Microsoft Copilot USL inclusion is subject to fair usage limits.
claims.quote: Usage is limited to fair usage limits. Microsoft reserves the right to update the limits as the product evolves, and new usage patterns emerge.

claims.claim: The billing page states generative answer responses incur charges outside its specified exception.
claims.quote: Agents incur charges for generative answer responses unless the agent is created in Agent Builder in Microsoft 365 and the response doesn't leverage tenant graph grounding.

claims.claim: The cited billing rates and management page describes agents using the standard harness.
claims.quote: This article describes features used in agents or agent flows powered by the standard harness.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness experiences charge Copilot Credits for tools, including knowledge and MCPs.
claims.quote: For experiences powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness, Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Indirect cost; Scope: Users and licences
claims.claim: Customer profile lookups require unified Customer Insights - Data profiles.
claims.quote: The customer profile tools don't read Customer Insights - Journeys data. If you use only Customer Insights - Journeys, there are no unified customer profiles for these tools to read.

claims.claim: Consent, journey and email tools do not need a unified customer ID.
claims.quote: The consent, journey, and email tools don't need a unified customer ID.

claims.claim: Consent tools need Customer Insights - Journeys or Shared Consent.
claims.quote: The journey and email tools need Customer Insights - Journeys, and the consent tools need Customer Insights - Journeys or Shared Consent.

claims.claim: Configuring the MCP server requires the System Administrator role.
claims.quote: The System Administrator role, to configure the MCP server

claims.claim: Retrying create_journey can create a duplicate journey.
claims.quote: It isn't idempotent, so retrying a failed call can create a duplicate journey. Have your agent confirm the outcome before it retries.

claims.where: Scope: Users and licences; What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Journey and email tools, including create_journey, require Customer Insights - Journeys.
claims.quote: The journey and email tools need Customer Insights - Journeys.

claims.claim: A data policy regulating Power Platform connectors regulates the MCP server and tools used by a Copilot Studio agent.
claims.quote: This condition means that if a data policy regulates Power Platform connectors, it also regulates access to the MCP server and its tools for your agent.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio MCP server access relies on Power Platform connectors for connectivity.
claims.quote: Access to MCP servers in Copilot Studio relies on Power Platform connectors for connectivity.

claims.claim: The cited Copilot Studio onboarding process is the same for prebuilt Microsoft MCP connectors and servers with a configured connection.
claims.quote: The process is the same, whether you're adding prebuilt Microsoft MCP connectors or an MCP server to which you configured a connection.

claims.where: Governance controls; Open questions: external-client data policies

No passage extends that policy to external gateway clients.

claims.claim: Registry Block and per-agent tool toggles do not document a selector for particular customer profiles or returned fields.
claims.quote: Searched: Customer Insights MCP restrict profiles fields attributes beyond Dataverse security roles. Read Tools overview, Copilot Studio tool toggles and Customer Insights tools reference; controls allow or block servers/tools, with no profile/field selector in either control.

claims.claim: Dataverse security-role privileges govern access to the data behind the server's tools.
claims.quote: Access to the Dataverse tables that back the tools you plan to call. The Dataverse security role privileges that the tools require for the user or agent identity.

claims.claim: The gateway service principal must exist in the customer tenant before a client app can request a gateway token.
claims.quote: Before a client app can request a token for it, the gateway service principal must exist in the customer tenant.

claims.claim: Granting admin consent on the configured client app puts McpServers.D365CustomerInsights.All into tokens requested by that client.
claims.quote: Granting admin consent here is what puts McpServers.D365CustomerInsights.All into the tokens your client requests.

claims.claim: The permission to check in a denied gateway token is McpServers.D365CustomerInsights.All in the scp claim.
claims.quote: If calls are denied, decode the token and check that the scp claim contains McpServers.D365CustomerInsights.All.
